I've never been an an avid reader (some periods in my life may have qualified me as such for a time) and it always makes me suspicious when I hear about how much people love books, how much they're constantly spending on them, and their analysis of various books I've never cracked. I feel like I spend too much money on books, but most of them I'll never lead, they're just passing obsessions that ended before they ever got off the ground. I have read a few important works, binging on some and hammering my way through others, and they helped me to become an mildly educated person who can at least employ fairly proper grammar, but on the whole I'm not well read and I probably never will be. I lost interest at a fairly young age. I got caught up in a few books, but after a little while, everything started to feel like more of the same. Yeah, it's a story, I've read lots of stories, what's so special about this one? It's just more of the same.

Yet every once in a while I'll come across something that will just really hook me and I don't know why. The last book to really hook me was quite fat fan fiction novel called Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality. The book has soo many flaws, yet I just ate it up, reading all day everyday until I had finished it. Perhaps it was its flaws that made it so attractive to me. The uniqueness of its flaws made it not simply more of the same. That's not to say that it didn't also have strengths, it had plenty of strengths mixed in with its faults.

Now I'm interested in Latin, but I have a hard time focusing on it because the distractions of modern life, Voat being at the forefront, are just too damn ever present. I'm trying to get away from everything so that I can study Latin in peace, but life is complicated, and often disconnected oneself isn't so easy as just pulling a plug. Nonetheless I'm slowly making progress and hope to get there eventually. Then maybe I'll be able to hammer through until I'm able to again get hooked and read all the great works of ancient authors to whom we own the foundation of our current civilization. I suppose I could just read them in English, but everything in English just feels like more of the same.

I was a voracious reader as a kid. A few years ago I realized that I had stopped reading, and I missed it , and I didn't want to be the kind of person that didn't read. I also found that my usual easy eloquence while speaking had become punctuated with pauses while I searched for the right word - I felt that the vocabulary I had ready access to was shrinking the longer I stayed away from reading what this author called "literature."

My solution was to subscribe to a few places that occasionally called out books that people generally thought were good and engaging, and install the Amazon app on my phone with one-click ordering. whenever I saw a book mentioned and I agreed with the summary and comments that it seemed like something I should read, I would impulse purchase it, and then two days later (thanks, Prime!) I'd have a surprise present.

I also made it a point to occasionally visit secondhand bookstores and paw through the dollar piles for anything that looked engaging.

The only people I know in the real world who also read books are my mother and one aunt. Most everyone else didn't read when they were little, stopped reading as soon as they could get away with it, and is completely unreceptive to any sales pitch I could make about any book, because they're not a book-reading person. Not only can I not talk to them about the books that I am reading now, but the idea of reading for pleasure is completely foreign to them. The author in the linked article has spent a lot more time thinking about and describing the situation that I have, but their analysis rings true.
